name: Jerusalem
eraNotes: Capital of Judah/Israel; Temple Mount area. Continuous habitation into the modern city.

name: Bethlehem
eraNotes: Judahite town south of Jerusalem; associated with David and Jesus’ birth narratives.

name: Nazareth
eraNotes: Galilean village; childhood home of Jesus in the Gospels.

name: Capernaum
eraNotes: Fishing town on the NW shore of the Sea of Galilee; base for Jesus’ Galilean ministry.

name: Sea of Galilee
eraNotes: Freshwater lake in northern Israel; setting for many Gospel scenes.

name: Jordan River
eraNotes: River forming much of the eastern edge of the biblical land; baptism of Jesus associated with its lower reaches.

name: Euphrates
eraNotes: Major Mesopotamian river; often marks the ideal northeastern reach of the promised land and appears in patriarchal and prophetic texts. Pin near the middle Euphrates corridor.

name: Jericho
eraNotes: Oasis city in the Jordan Valley; associated with Joshua’s conquest and NT visits.

name: Hebron
eraNotes: Patriarchal city; burial tradition at Machpelah.

name: Beersheba
eraNotes: Southern landmark of Israelite territory; patriarchal wells tradition.

name: Shechem
modernName: Nablus / Tell Balata area, West Bank
eraNotes: Central hill-country city; Jacob and Joseph traditions; nearby Sychar in John.

name: Bethel
eraNotes: Important sanctuary site in patriarchal and Israelite narratives.

name: Ai
eraNotes: Town associated with Joshua’s campaigns east of Bethel.

name: Shiloh
eraNotes: Early Israelite cult center; Tabernacle tradition before Jerusalem.

name: Tirzah
eraNotes: Early capital of the northern kingdom (Jeroboam and successors) before Samaria.

name: Megiddo
eraNotes: Strategic Jezreel Valley fortress; later apocalyptic association.

name: Hazor
eraNotes: Major Canaanite/Israelite city in Upper Galilee.

name: Dan
eraNotes: Northern city (ex-Laish) and boundary marker; bare 'Dan' is not matched — it is usually the person/tribe.

name: Caesarea
eraNotes: Herodian port and Roman capital of Judea; key Acts setting.

name: Caesarea Philippi
eraNotes: Northern city at Hermon springs; Peter’s confession setting.

name: Joppa
eraNotes: Mediterranean port; Jonah and Peter traditions.

name: Ashkelon
eraNotes: Philistine coastal city.

name: Gaza
eraNotes: Philistine city; Samson and Acts road traditions.

name: Ashdod
eraNotes: Philistine city; Azotus in Acts.

name: Gath
eraNotes: Philistine city associated with Goliath.

name: Ekron
eraNotes: Philistine city; Ark narrative.

name: Samaria
eraNotes: Capital of the northern kingdom; later Sebaste.

name: Emmaus
eraNotes: Village associated with the post-resurrection road story; location debated.

name: Bethany
eraNotes: Village near Jerusalem; Lazarus tradition. Distinct from Bethany-beyond-Jordan debates.

name: Bethsaida
eraNotes: Fishing town near the Sea of Galilee; exact site debated.

name: Chorazin
eraNotes: Galilean town rebuked with Bethsaida and Capernaum.

name: Cana
eraNotes: Wedding at Cana tradition; site identification debated.

name: Nain
eraNotes: Village south of Nazareth; raising of the widow’s son.

name: Sidon
eraNotes: Phoenician coastal city.

name: Tyre
eraNotes: Phoenician island/coastal city; prophetic and NT connections.

name: Damascus
eraNotes: Aramean capital; Paul’s conversion road tradition.

name: Antioch
eraNotes: Major Hellenistic city; early Christian mission hub in Acts.

name: Antioch of Pisidia
eraNotes: Roman colony visited on Paul’s first missionary journey.

name: Tarsus
eraNotes: Cilician city; Paul’s hometown.

name: Iconium
eraNotes: City on Paul’s first missionary journey.

name: Lystra
eraNotes: Lycaonian town; Timothy’s home region.

name: Derbe
eraNotes: Lycaonian town on Paul’s first journey.

name: Perga
eraNotes: Pamphylian city visited early on Paul’s journeys.

name: Attalia
eraNotes: Pamphylian port; return harbor after first journey.

name: Seleucia
eraNotes: Port of Antioch from which Paul and Barnabas sailed.

name: Salamis
eraNotes: Eastern Cypriot city; first stop after sailing from Seleucia.

name: Paphos
eraNotes: Western Cypriot city; encounter with Sergius Paulus.

name: Ephesus
eraNotes: Major Asian metropolis; long Pauline stay; Artemis cult.

name: Smyrna
eraNotes: Asian coastal city; one of the seven churches of Revelation.

name: Pergamum
eraNotes: Asian city; one of the seven churches of Revelation.

name: Thyatira
eraNotes: Lydian city; Lydia of Thyatira in Acts; Revelation church.

name: Sardis
eraNotes: Former Lydian capital; Revelation church.

name: Philadelphia
eraNotes: Asian city; one of the seven churches of Revelation.

name: Laodicea
eraNotes: Wealthy Lycus Valley city; Revelation church.

name: Colossae
eraNotes: Phrygian town; letter to the Colossians.

name: Troas
eraNotes: Aegean port; Macedonian call vision.

name: Philippi
eraNotes: Roman colony in Macedonia; first European church tradition.

name: Thessalonica
eraNotes: Macedonian capital; Pauline letters.

name: Berea
eraNotes: Macedonian city praised for examining the Scriptures.

name: Athens
eraNotes: Greek cultural center; Areopagus speech.

name: Corinth
eraNotes: Major Achaian city; long Pauline ministry; Corinthian letters.

name: Cenchreae
eraNotes: Eastern port of Corinth; Phoebe’s church.

name: Rome
eraNotes: Imperial capital; destination of Paul’s appeal; letter to the Romans.

name: Puteoli
eraNotes: Italian port where Paul landed en route to Rome.

name: Malta
eraNotes: Island of Paul’s shipwreck in Acts 27–28.

name: Fair Havens
eraNotes: Harbor on Crete during Paul’s voyage to Rome.

name: Myra
eraNotes: Lycian port; ship transfer on the voyage to Rome.

name: Memphis
eraNotes: Ancient Egyptian capital region referenced in prophetic literature.

name: Thebes
eraNotes: Upper Egyptian capital; prophetic oracles against No-Amon.

name: Rameses
eraNotes: Store-city and traditional Exodus departure region.

name: Succoth
eraNotes: First Exodus encampment after leaving Rameses; exact site debated.

name: Etham
modernName: Edge of the wilderness near the Isthmus of Suez
eraNotes: Exodus staging point before the sea crossing traditions.

name: Pi-hahiroth
modernName: Northern Red Sea / Bitter Lakes region (debated)
eraNotes: Campsite before the sea crossing; geography debated.

name: Marah
eraNotes: First wilderness water crisis after the sea.

name: Elim
eraNotes: Oasis with springs and palms in Exodus itinerary.

name: Rephidim
eraNotes: Site of water from the rock and Amalek conflict traditions.

name: Mount Sinai
modernName: Jebel Musa tradition, South Sinai, Egypt
eraNotes: Traditional mountain of the covenant; alternative Horeb/Sinai proposals exist.

name: Kadesh-barnea
eraNotes: Major wilderness staging area; spy narrative and long sojourn traditions.

name: Ezion-geber
eraNotes: Red Sea port region associated with wilderness itinerary and later trade.

name: Plains of Moab
modernName: East of the Jordan opposite Jericho, Jordan
eraNotes: Final wilderness camp before crossing into Canaan.

name: Ur
eraNotes: Traditional starting point of Abraham’s migration.

name: Haran
eraNotes: Upper Mesopotamian city; Abraham’s family sojourn.

name: Egypt
eraNotes: Nile civilization; patriarchal sojourns and Exodus setting. Map pin uses Cairo-region coordinates.

name: Canaan
eraNotes: Promised land region in patriarchal and conquest narratives.

name: Babylon
eraNotes: Mesopotamian capital; exile destination and prophetic oracles.

name: Nineveh
eraNotes: Assyrian capital; Jonah narrative.

name: Susa
eraNotes: Persian royal city; Esther and Nehemiah settings.

name: Persia
eraNotes: Imperial setting for later OT narratives; marker near Persepolis.

name: Patmos
eraNotes: Aegean island of John’s exile in Revelation.

name: Gilgal
eraNotes: Early Israelite camp after crossing the Jordan.

name: Mizpah
eraNotes: Benjaminite assembly site; multiple Mizpahs exist in the text.

name: Gibeah
eraNotes: Benjaminite town associated with Saul.

name: Ramah
eraNotes: Benjaminite town; Samuel and exile-road traditions.

name: En-gedi
eraNotes: Oasis on the western Dead Sea; David’s wilderness refuge.

name: Dead Sea
eraNotes: Hypersaline lake; biblical Salt Sea.

name: Mount of Olives
eraNotes: Ridge east of Jerusalem; key Gospel settings.

name: Golgotha
modernName: Church of the Holy Sepulchre / Gordon's Calvary area, Jerusalem
eraNotes: Traditional crucifixion site; exact spot debated within Jerusalem.

name: Bethphage
modernName: Mount of Olives eastern slope, Jerusalem
eraNotes: Village near Bethany on the approach to Jerusalem.

name: Zarephath
eraNotes: Phoenician coastal town between Tyre and Sidon; Elijah and the widow (1 Kings 17).

name: Mount Carmel
eraNotes: Coastal ridge; Elijah’s contest with the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18).

name: Jezreel
eraNotes: Royal city in the Jezreel Valley; Ahab/Jezebel and Elijah narratives.

name: Brook Cherith
eraNotes: Wadi east of the Jordan where Elijah hid and was fed by ravens (1 Kings 17). Exact site uncertain.

name: Ophir
modernName: Location debated (often South Arabia / Horn of Africa traditions)
eraNotes: Source of gold for Solomon’s fleet (1 Kings 9). Pin uses a Sabaean/South Arabian teaching location.

name: Sheba
eraNotes: Homeland of the Queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10). Exact locale debated (Arabia or Horn of Africa).

name: Penuel
eraNotes: Jacob’s Peniel tradition; later fortified by Jeroboam (1 Kings 12).

name: Aphek
modernName: Fiq / Aphek region, Golan (1 Kings 20 tradition)
eraNotes: Town where Aramean forces fled after battle with Ahab (1 Kings 20). Several biblical Apheks exist.

name: Kidron Valley
eraNotes: Valley east of Jerusalem between the Temple Mount and Mount of Olives; Asa burned Maacah’s Asherah pole here (1 Kings 15).

name: Aram
eraNotes: Aramean kingdom north of Israel; Ben-hadad’s realm in 1 Kings 15. NLT “Aram”; many English Bibles “Syria”.

name: Ijon
eraNotes: Northern Israelite town taken by Ben-hadad for Asa (1 Kings 15:20).

name: Abel-beth-maacah
eraNotes: Northern border town near Dan; captured by Ben-hadad (1 Kings 15:20).

name: Naphtali
eraNotes: Northern tribal territory; Ben-hadad struck “all the land of Naphtali” (1 Kings 15:20).

name: Geba
eraNotes: Benjaminite town fortified by Asa with stones from Ramah (1 Kings 15:22).

name: Gibbethon
modernName: Tel Malot / Tell el-Melat area, Israel (debated)
eraNotes: Philistine town Nadab was besieging when Baasha killed him (1 Kings 15:27).

name: Tishbe
modernName: Listib / el-Istib area near Ajloun, Jordan (traditional; exact site debated)
eraNotes: Hometown of Elijah the Tishbite (1 Kings 17:1). Traditional identification near Mar Elias / Listib in Gilead; Iron Age site uncertain.

name: Gilead
modernName: Highlands east of the Jordan, Jordan
eraNotes: Transjordan region where Elijah was from (Tishbe in Gilead). Also associated with Jabesh-gilead, Ramoth-gilead, and other towns.

name: Abarim
modernName: Mountain range east of the Dead Sea, Jordan
eraNotes: Camp before Nebo (Num 33:47); Moses' viewing range (Num 27:12; Deut 32:49).

name: Acco
eraNotes: Asher fails to expel (Judg 1:31). 'Ptolemais' (Acts 21:7) is flagged missing in the coverage inventory.

name: Achzib
eraNotes: Asher (Josh 19:29; Judg 1:31). Josh 15:44 Achzib (= Chezib, Gen 38:5) is a Judahite town.

name: Adam (city)
eraNotes: Jordan waters heap up (Josh 3:16). Bare 'Adam' must never be an alias.

name: Adullam
eraNotes: Judah's friend Hirah (Gen 38:1); Canaanite king (Josh 12:15); later David's cave.

name: Aijalon
eraNotes: Moon stands still (Josh 10:12); Danite/Levitical (Josh 19:42; 21:24); Judg 1:35. Judg 12:12 Aijalon is in Zebulun.

name: Ammon
eraNotes: Lot's descendants (Gen 19:38); border on the Jabbok (Deut 2:19,37); Jephthah (Judg 10-11).

name: Anathoth
modernName: Ras el-Kharrubeh near Anata, West Bank
eraNotes: Levitical city (Josh 21:18). Later Jeremiah.

name: Arabah
eraNotes: Rift valley south (and north) of the Dead Sea (Deut 1:1,7; 2:8; Josh 11:2; 12:1). 'Sea of the Arabah' already maps to dead_sea.

name: Arad
eraNotes: King of Arad attacks Israel (Num 21:1); defeated (Josh 12:14); Kenites settle nearby (Judg 1:16). Bronze Age Arad may be Tel Malhata.

name: Aram-naharaim
eraNotes: Region of Nahor's city (Gen 24:10, ESV 'Mesopotamia'); Balaam's home (Deut 23:4); Cushan-rishathaim (Judg 3:8).

name: Mountains of Ararat
eraNotes: Ark comes to rest (Gen 8:4). Biblical Ararat = Urartu region; pin at traditional peak.

name: Arnon
eraNotes: Moab/Amorite border (Num 21:13; Deut 2:24; Judg 11:18).

name: Aroer
eraNotes: On the rim of the Arnon (Deut 2:36; Josh 12:2; 13:9; Judg 11:26). Other Aroers: Gad (Josh 13:25), Judah (1 Sam 30:28).

name: Ashtaroth
eraNotes: Rephaim defeated (Gen 14:5); Og's capital (Deut 1:4; Josh 12:4). In Judges 2:13; 10:6 'the Ashtaroth' are goddesses — alias risk.

name: Assyria
eraNotes: Pinned at Ashur, the old Assyrian capital. 'Asshur' is also a son of Shem (Gen 10:22).

name: Ataroth
eraNotes: Built by Gad (Num 32:3,34). Josh 16:2,5,7 Ataroth/Ataroth-addar is a different Ephraimite site.

name: Azekah
eraNotes: Pursuit ends (Josh 10:10-11); Judah town (Josh 15:35). Later Goliath (1 Sam 17).

name: Bashan
eraNotes: Og's kingdom (Num 21:33; Deut 3); given to half-Manasseh (Josh 13:30).

name: Beth-horon
eraNotes: Pass of the rout (Josh 10:10-11); Ephraim border (Josh 16:3,5); Levitical (Josh 21:22).

name: Beth-jeshimoth
eraNotes: Southern end of the Moab camp (Num 33:49; Josh 12:3; 13:20).

name: Beth-shean
eraNotes: Manasseh fails to expel (Josh 17:11,16; Judg 1:27). Later Saul's body.

name: Beth-shemesh
eraNotes: Judah border/Levitical (Josh 15:10; 21:16); Danite Ir-shemesh (Josh 19:41); Judg 1:33 Beth-shemesh is in Naphtali.

name: Beth-zur
eraNotes: Josh 15:58.

name: Bezek
eraNotes: Adoni-bezek defeated (Judg 1:4-5; possibly a different Judahite site). Saul's muster (1 Sam 11:8).

name: Bozrah
eraNotes: Edomite royal city (Gen 36:33).

name: Brook of Egypt
eraNotes: SW border of the promised land (Num 34:5; Josh 15:4). Gen 15:18 'river of Egypt' is sometimes read as the Nile.

name: Cabul
eraNotes: Asher (Josh 19:27). Later Solomon's gift to Hiram.

name: Calah
eraNotes: Built by Nimrod/Asshur (Gen 10:11-12).

name: Caphtor
eraNotes: Origin of the Caphtorim/Philistines (Deut 2:23).

name: Chephirah
eraNotes: Gibeonite city (Josh 9:17; 18:26).

name: Daberath
eraNotes: Josh 19:12; Levitical (Josh 21:28).

name: Dibon
eraNotes: Num 21:30; 32:34; 33:45 (Dibon-gad). Mesha Stele found here.

name: Dothan
eraNotes: Joseph sold by his brothers (Gen 37:17).

name: Mount Ebal
eraNotes: Curses and altar (Deut 11:29; 27:4,13; Josh 8:30). 'Ebal' is also an Edomite name (Gen 36:23).

name: Edom
eraNotes: Esau's nation (Gen 36); refuses Israel passage (Num 20:14-21). In Gen 25:30; 36:1,8,19 'Edom' is Esau's name.

name: Edrei
eraNotes: Og defeated (Num 21:33; Deut 3:1). Josh 19:37 Edrei is a different town in Naphtali.

name: Elam
eraNotes: Kedorlaomer's kingdom (Gen 14). 'Elam' is also a son of Shem (Gen 10:22).

name: Elath
eraNotes: Passed on the Arabah road (Deut 2:8).

name: En-gannim
eraNotes: Issachar/Levitical (Josh 19:21; 21:29). Josh 15:34 En-gannim is in Judah.

name: En-rogel
eraNotes: Boundary marker (Josh 15:7; 18:16). Later Adonijah's feast.

name: Endor
eraNotes: Manasseh in Issachar (Josh 17:11). Later Saul's medium.

name: Erech
eraNotes: City of Nimrod's kingdom (Gen 10:10).

name: Eshtemoa
eraNotes: Josh 15:50; Levitical (Josh 21:14).

name: Gath-hepher
eraNotes: Zebulun (Josh 19:13). Jonah's hometown (2 Kgs 14:25).

name: Gebal
eraNotes: 'Land of the Gebalites' (Josh 13:5).

name: Gerar
eraNotes: Abimelech's city (Gen 20; 26).

name: Mount Gerizim
eraNotes: Blessings (Deut 11:29; 27:12; Josh 8:33); Jotham's fable (Judg 9:7).

name: Gezer
eraNotes: King Horam defeated (Josh 10:33); Canaanites remain (Josh 16:10; Judg 1:29).

name: Gibeon
eraNotes: Gibeonite treaty (Josh 9); sun stands still (Josh 10:12); Levitical (Josh 21:17).

name: Goshen
modernName: Wadi Tumilat / eastern Nile Delta, Egypt
eraNotes: Israel's settlement in Egypt (Gen 45:10; 47; Exod 8:22; 9:26). Josh 10:41; 11:16; 15:51 'Goshen' is a district/town in Judah.

name: Mediterranean Sea
eraNotes: Western boundary (Exod 23:31; Num 34:6; Josh 1:4; 15:12).

name: Halhul
eraNotes: Josh 15:58.

name: Hammath
eraNotes: Naphtali (Josh 19:35; 21:32).

name: Spring of Harod
eraNotes: Gideon tests the 300 (Judg 7:1).

name: Mount Hermon
eraNotes: Northern limit of conquest (Deut 3:8-9; Josh 11:17; 12:1; 13:5; Judg 3:3).

name: Heshbon
eraNotes: Sihon's capital (Num 21:26); Reuben/Gad (Num 32:37); Levitical (Josh 21:39).

name: Hill Country of Ephraim
eraNotes: Joshua's burial (Josh 24:30); Deborah (Judg 4:5); Micah (Judg 17:1); the Levite (Judg 19:1).

name: Hill of Moreh
eraNotes: Midianite camp (Judg 7:1).

name: Ibleam
eraNotes: Josh 17:11; Judg 1:27.

name: Jabbok
eraNotes: Jacob wrestles (Gen 32:22); Ammonite/Amorite border (Num 21:24; Deut 3:16).

name: Jabneel
eraNotes: Judah's NW border (Josh 15:11). Josh 19:33 Jabneel is in Naphtali.

name: Japhia
eraNotes: Zebulun border (Josh 19:12).

name: Jarmuth
eraNotes: Amorite king Piram (Josh 10:3). Josh 21:29 Jarmuth is in Issachar.

name: Jattir
eraNotes: Josh 15:48; Levitical (Josh 21:14).

name: Jogbehah
eraNotes: Built by Gad (Num 32:35); Gideon's route (Judg 8:11).

name: Kedesh
eraNotes: Canaanite king (Josh 12:22); city of refuge (Josh 20:7); Barak's home (Judg 4:6). Judg 4:9-11 Kedesh may be a site near the Sea of Galilee.

name: Keilah
eraNotes: Josh 15:44. Later rescued by David.

name: Kenath
eraNotes: Taken by Nobah and renamed (Num 32:42).

name: Kiriath-jearim
eraNotes: Gibeonite city (Josh 9:17); Judah/Benjamin border (Josh 15:9; 18:14); Danite camp (Judg 18:12). Later ark resting place.

name: Kishon
eraNotes: Sisera's army swept away (Judg 4:7,13; 5:21). Later Elijah (1 Kgs 18:40).

name: Kittim
eraNotes: Ships from Kittim (Num 24:24).

name: Cyprus
eraNotes: Eastern Mediterranean island; Barnabas's home; Paul's first journey landfall (Salamis → Paphos).

name: Lachish
eraNotes: Taken by Joshua (Josh 10:31-32). Later Sennacherib's siege.

name: Lebanon
eraNotes: Northern horizon of the promise (Deut 1:7; 3:25; Josh 1:4; 13:5; Judg 3:3).

name: Lebo-hamath
eraNotes: Northern limit of the spies (Num 13:21) and of the land (Num 34:8; Josh 13:5; Judg 3:3).

name: Lebonah
eraNotes: Locates Shiloh (Judg 21:19).

name: Cave of Machpelah
eraNotes: Purchased by Abraham (Gen 23); patriarchal tomb (Gen 25, 49, 50).

name: Mahanaim
eraNotes: Jacob meets angels (Gen 32:2); Levitical city of Gad (Josh 21:38). Later Ish-bosheth's / David's base.

name: Mamre
eraNotes: Abraham's camp (Gen 13:18; 18:1). Mamre is also an Amorite ally's name (Gen 14:13).

name: Maon
eraNotes: Josh 15:55. Later Nabal / Wilderness of Maon.

name: Mareshah
eraNotes: Josh 15:44.

name: Midian
eraNotes: Moses' refuge (Exod 2:15); Balaam/Peor (Num 25; 31); Gideon (Judg 6-8). 'Midian' is also a son of Abraham (Gen 25:2).

name: Moriah
eraNotes: Binding of Isaac (Gen 22:2); equated with the Temple Mount in 2 Chr 3:1.

name: Mount Nebo
eraNotes: Moses dies (Deut 32:49; 34:1). Also a Reubenite town (Num 32:38) and a Babylonian god (Isa 46:1).

name: Negeb
eraNotes: Southern dry country; Abraham's route (Gen 12:9; 13:1); spies (Num 13).

name: Nile
eraNotes: Moses in the basket (Exod 2:3); first plague (Exod 7). Pharaoh's dreams (Gen 41).

name: On (Heliopolis)
eraNotes: Asenath's father Potiphera 'priest of On' (Gen 41:45,50; 46:20). Bare 'On' is in BLOCKED_ALIASES, so the phrase alias is used.

name: Ophrah (Benjamin)
eraNotes: Benjamite town (Josh 18:23). Gideon's Ophrah (Judg 6-9) is a different, unlocated Manassite town.

name: Paddan-aram
eraNotes: Laban's homeland around Haran (Gen 25:20; 28:2; 31:18; 48:7).

name: Wilderness of Paran
eraNotes: Ishmael's home (Gen 21:21); camp after Sinai (Num 10:12; 12:16). Region pin.

name: Philistia
eraNotes: 'Way of the land of the Philistines' (Exod 13:17); Gerar's Philistines (Gen 21; 26); five lords (Josh 13:3); Samson (Judg 13-16).

name: Pisgah
eraNotes: Balaam's second oracle (Num 23:14); Moses views the land (Deut 3:27; 34:1).

name: Pithom
eraNotes: Store city built by Israel (Exod 1:11). Alternative: Tell el-Maskhuta.

name: Punon
eraNotes: Wilderness camp (Num 33:42-43).

name: Rabbah
aliases: Rabbah of the children of Ammon
eraNotes: Og's iron bed kept here (Deut 3:11); Gad's border (Josh 13:25). Josh 15:60 Rabbah is a Judahite village.

name: Ramoth-gilead
eraNotes: City of refuge (Deut 4:43; Josh 20:8; 21:38); Ahab's death (1 Kgs 22). Also named as missing in the coverage inventory.

name: Red Sea
modernName: Gulf of Suez (pin); also the Gulf of Aqaba
eraNotes: Locusts driven into it (Exod 10:19); sea crossing (Exod 13:18; 15:4). 'Red Sea' also names the Gulf of Aqaba (Num 21:4; Deut 2:1; 1 Kgs 9:26). Crossing site debated.

name: Riblah
eraNotes: NE border marker (Num 34:11; reading debated). Later Nebuchadnezzar's HQ (2 Kgs 25:6).

name: Salecah
eraNotes: Eastern edge of Bashan (Deut 3:10; Josh 12:5; 13:11).

name: Seir
eraNotes: Esau's territory (Gen 32:3; 36:8); Israel skirts it (Deut 2). Also Seir the Horite (Gen 36:20).

name: Shaalbim
eraNotes: Josh 19:42; Judg 1:35.

name: Shephelah
eraNotes: Lowland district (Josh 10:40; 15:33). ESV often translates 'the lowland', which is too generic to alias.

name: Shimron
eraNotes: Joined Jabin's coalition (Josh 11:1; 12:20).

name: Shinar
eraNotes: Plain of Babel (Gen 11:2); Amraphel's kingdom (Gen 14); Achan's cloak (Josh 7:21).

name: Shittim
eraNotes: Peor apostasy (Num 25:1); spies sent from here (Josh 2:1; 3:1).

name: Shunem
eraNotes: Issachar (Josh 19:18). Later Elisha / Philistine camp.

name: Wilderness of Shur
eraNotes: Desert east of Egypt (Gen 16:7; 20:1; 25:18; Exod 15:22). Region pin.

name: Socoh
eraNotes: Shephelah town (Josh 15:35); a second Socoh in the hill country (Josh 15:48).

name: Mount Tabor
eraNotes: Border (Josh 19:22); Barak's muster (Judg 4:6,12,14); Judg 8:18.

name: Tigris
eraNotes: Third river of Eden (Gen 2:14); Daniel 10:4.

name: Timnah
eraNotes: Samson's wife (Judg 14); Dan/Judah border (Josh 15:10; 19:43). Gen 38:12 Timnah may be a different hill-country site (Josh 15:57).

name: Timnath-serah
eraNotes: Joshua's inheritance and burial (Josh 19:50; 24:30; Judg 2:9).

name: Valley of Hinnom
aliases: Valley of the Son of Hinnom
eraNotes: Judah/Benjamin boundary (Josh 15:8; 18:16). Later Topheth/Gehenna.

name: Valley of Rephaim
eraNotes: Boundary (Josh 15:8; 18:16). Later David vs Philistines.

name: Valley of Sorek
eraNotes: Delilah's home (Judg 16:4).

name: Wilderness of Judah
eraNotes: Kenites settle (Judg 1:16). Later David.

name: Wilderness of Sin
eraNotes: Manna and quail (Exod 16:1). Never alias bare 'Sin'.

name: Wilderness of Zin
eraNotes: Kadesh lies in Zin (Num 20:1; 33:36); southern border (Num 34:3; Josh 15:1). Distinct from Wilderness of Sin.

name: Brook Zered
eraNotes: Edom/Moab border crossed (Num 21:12; Deut 2:13-14).

name: Ziph
eraNotes: Josh 15:55 (also a Negeb Ziph, 15:24). Later David's hideout.

name: Zoan
eraNotes: Built seven years after Hebron (Num 13:22).

name: Zoar
eraNotes: Lot's refuge (Gen 19). Also called Bela (Gen 14:2,8) — 'Bela' omitted as alias (also a personal name).

name: Zorah
eraNotes: Samson's birthplace (Judg 13:2); Danite scouts (Judg 18:2).

name: Ebenezer
eraNotes: Israel's camp when the ark was captured (1 Sam 4); later Samuel's memorial stone (1 Sam 7:12, likely a different spot).

name: Aphek (Sharon)
eraNotes: Philistine muster point at the Yarkon springs (1 Sam 4:1; 29:1); later Herodian Antipatris (Acts 23:31).

name: Rachel's Tomb
modernName: Traditional site at Bethlehem; 1 Sam 10 implies a Benjamin-border location
eraNotes: Sign to Saul at Zelzah on the border of Benjamin (1 Sam 10:2).

name: Jabesh-gilead
eraNotes: Rescued by Saul from Nahash (1 Sam 11); its men recover Saul's body from Beth-shan (1 Sam 31).

name: Michmash
eraNotes: Philistine camp opposite Geba; Jonathan's cliff assault (1 Sam 13-14).

name: Beth-aven
eraNotes: Battle line passes Beth-aven (1 Sam 13:5; 14:23); Hosea's slur for Bethel.

name: Carmel (Judah)
eraNotes: Saul's victory monument (1 Sam 15:12); Nabal's estate (1 Sam 25). Distinct from Mount Carmel.

name: Amalek
eraNotes: Nomadic foe of the Negev/Sinai; Saul's campaign (1 Sam 15); David's raids and pursuit (1 Sam 27, 30).

name: Cush
eraNotes: Nubian kingdom: Zerah (2 Chr 14), Tirhakah (2 Kgs 19:9).

name: Valley of Elah
eraNotes: David kills Goliath (1 Sam 17).

name: Nob
eraNotes: City of priests; Ahimelech gives David bread and Goliath's sword; massacred by Doeg (1 Sam 21-22).

name: Ziklag
eraNotes: Given to David by Achish; burned by Amalekites (1 Sam 27; 30).

name: Mount Gilboa
eraNotes: Saul and Jonathan die (1 Sam 31; 2 Sam 1; 1 Chr 10).

name: Brook Besor
eraNotes: 200 exhausted men stay behind in the Amalekite pursuit (1 Sam 30:9-10).

name: Aroer (Negeb)
eraNotes: One of the towns receiving David's spoil (1 Sam 30:28). Distinct from Aroer by the Arnon.

name: Hormah
eraNotes: Receives David's spoil (1 Sam 30:30); Simeonite town (1 Chr 4:30).

name: Bahurim
eraNotes: Shimei curses David; spies hide in a well (2 Sam 16-17).

name: Beeroth
eraNotes: Home of Ish-bosheth's assassins (2 Sam 4:2).

name: Geshur
modernName: Golan / NE of Sea of Galilee
eraNotes: Aramean kingdom of Talmai, Absalom's grandfather; Absalom's exile (2 Sam 13-15).

name: Baal-perazim
eraNotes: David's breakthrough over the Philistines (2 Sam 5:20).

name: Zobah
eraNotes: Hadadezer's Aramean kingdom defeated by David (2 Sam 8; 10); Rezon's origin (1 Kgs 11:23).

name: Hamath
eraNotes: Toi's tribute to David; Jeroboam II; deportees to Samaria; Riblah 'in the land of Hamath'.

name: Valley of Salt
modernName: Arabah south of the Dead Sea (debated)
eraNotes: Edomites defeated by David/Abishai (2 Sam 8:13; 1 Chr 18:12) and by Amaziah (2 Kgs 14:7).

name: Lo-debar
eraNotes: Mephibosheth's home (2 Sam 9:4); Machir supplies David (2 Sam 17:27).

name: Maacah
eraNotes: Aramean kingdom hired by Ammon (2 Sam 10:6; 1 Chr 19:6-7).

name: Tob
eraNotes: Mercenaries hired by Ammon (2 Sam 10:6).

name: Helam
eraNotes: David defeats Hadadezer's coalition (2 Sam 10:16-17).

name: Baal-hazor
eraNotes: Absalom kills Amnon at the sheep-shearing (2 Sam 13:23).

name: Tekoa
eraNotes: Wise woman (2 Sam 14); Rehoboam fort; Jehoshaphat's army marches out (2 Chr 20:20); Amos's home.

name: Gihon Spring
eraNotes: Solomon anointed (1 Kgs 1:33-45); Hezekiah's tunnel source (2 Chr 32:30).

name: Forest of Ephraim
eraNotes: Absalom's army defeated; Absalom killed (2 Sam 18:6-17). In Gilead.

name: Rogelim
eraNotes: Home of Barzillai the Gileadite (2 Sam 17:27; 19:31).

name: Netophah
eraNotes: Home of David's mighty men Maharai and Heleb; Levite villages (1 Chr 9:16).

name: Jazer
eraNotes: Census route (2 Sam 24:5); Levitical city in Gilead (1 Chr 6:81; 26:31).

name: Zarethan
eraNotes: Temple bronzes cast in the clay ground nearby (1 Kgs 7:46; 'Zeredah' in 2 Chr 4:17).

name: Succoth (Jordan Valley)
eraNotes: Bronze-casting ground for Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 7:46; 2 Chr 4:17). Distinct from Exodus Succoth.

name: Abel-meholah
eraNotes: Solomon's district (1 Kgs 4:12); Elisha's home where Elijah calls him (1 Kgs 19:16-19).

name: Baalath
eraNotes: Store city built by Solomon (1 Kgs 9:18; 2 Chr 8:6).

name: Tamar (wilderness)
eraNotes: Solomon's fortress in the Judean wilderness/Arabah (1 Kgs 9:18).

name: Tadmor
eraNotes: Desert city built by Solomon (2 Chr 8:4).

name: Tarshish
eraNotes: Distant western port; 'ships of Tarshish' (1 Kgs 10:22; 22:48; 2 Chr 9:21; 20:36).

name: Kue
eraNotes: Cilician horse market for Solomon (1 Kgs 10:28; 2 Chr 1:16).

name: Zeredah
eraNotes: Jeroboam's hometown in Ephraim (1 Kgs 11:26).

name: Kir-hareseth
eraNotes: Mesha's last stand; sacrifice of his son (2 Kgs 3:25-27).

name: Baal-shalishah
eraNotes: Firstfruits bread brought to Elisha (2 Kgs 4:42); Saul's donkey search (1 Sam 9:4).

name: Abana River
eraNotes: Naaman's boast about Damascus rivers (2 Kgs 5:12).

name: Pharpar River
eraNotes: Second river of Damascus (2 Kgs 5:12).

name: Libnah
eraNotes: Revolts under Joram (2 Kgs 8:22); Sennacherib besieges it (2 Kgs 19:8); Hamutal's town.

name: Sela
eraNotes: Edomite rock-fortress taken by Amaziah (2 Kgs 14:7; 2 Chr 25:12).

name: Tiphsah
eraNotes: Euphrates crossing marking Solomon's NE limit (1 Kgs 4:24). 2 Kgs 15:16 Tiphsah is probably a different town near Tirzah (Tappuah?).

name: Galilee
eraNotes: Cities given to Hiram (1 Kgs 9:11); conquered by Tiglath-pileser (2 Kgs 15:29). Also needed for the Gospels.

name: Kir
modernName: Unknown; placed near Elam per Isa 22:6
eraNotes: Where Damascenes were deported (2 Kgs 16:9).

name: Halah
eraNotes: Israelite exiles settled (2 Kgs 17:6; 18:11; 1 Chr 5:26).

name: Gozan
eraNotes: Israelite exiles on the Habor (2 Kgs 17:6); Assyrian conquest boast (2 Kgs 19:12).

name: Media
eraNotes: Israelite exiles in the cities of the Medes (2 Kgs 17:6; 18:11).

name: Cuthah
eraNotes: Settlers brought to Samaria (2 Kgs 17:24, 30).

name: Sepharvaim
eraNotes: Settlers to Samaria; Rabshakeh's boast (2 Kgs 17:24; 18:34).

name: Arpad
eraNotes: Conquered city in Rabshakeh's boast (2 Kgs 18:34; 19:13).

name: Rezeph
eraNotes: In Sennacherib's list of conquests (2 Kgs 19:12).

name: Carchemish
eraNotes: Neco's objective on the Euphrates (2 Chr 35:20).

name: Etam
eraNotes: Rehoboam fort (2 Chr 11:6); Judahite clan town (1 Chr 4:3).

name: Adoraim
eraNotes: Rehoboam fort (2 Chr 11:9).

name: Mount Zemaraim
eraNotes: Abijah's speech before battle with Jeroboam (2 Chr 13:4).

name: Jeshanah
eraNotes: Taken by Abijah with Bethel and Ephron (2 Chr 13:19).

name: Valley of Beracah
eraNotes: Jehoshaphat's thanksgiving after the coalition self-destructs (2 Chr 20:26).

name: Golan
eraNotes: Levitical city of refuge in Bashan (1 Chr 6:71).

name: Ashtaroth (Bashan)
eraNotes: Levitical city in Bashan (1 Chr 6:71).

name: Debir
eraNotes: Levitical city of Judah (1 Chr 6:58).

name: Ono
eraNotes: Built by Benjamite Shemed with Lod (1 Chr 8:12).

name: Lod
eraNotes: Built by Benjamite Shemed (1 Chr 8:12); Peter heals Aeneas (Acts 9).

name: Sharon
eraNotes: Gadite pasturelands (1 Chr 5:16); David's herds (1 Chr 27:29).

name: Valley of Achor
eraNotes: 'Door of hope' (Hos 2:15; Isa 65:10; Josh 7:24–26).

name: Alexandria
eraNotes: Synagogue of Alexandrians (Acts 6:9); Apollos (Acts 18:24); grain ships (Acts 27:6, 28:11).

name: Arabia
eraNotes: Arab lands (Isa 21:13; Jer 25:24; Ezek 27:21). In Gal 1:17 and 4:25 probably the Nabataean kingdom.

name: Arvad
eraNotes: Phoenician island city (Ezek 27:8, 11).

name: Benjamin (territory)
eraNotes: Tribal territory (Anathoth, Gibeah, Ramah, Mizpah); Jer 1:1, 17:26, 32:8, 32:44, 33:13, 37:12.

name: Berothah
eraNotes: Northern border point (Ezek 47:16).

name: Beth-eden
eraNotes: Aramean state Bit-Adini (Amos 1:5; 'children of Eden', Isa 37:12; Ezek 27:23). Not the garden of Eden.

name: Beth-gamul
eraNotes: Moabite town (Jer 48:23).

name: Beth-haccherem
eraNotes: Signal-fire station south of Jerusalem (Jer 6:1).

name: Bubastis (Pi-beseth)
eraNotes: Delta city (Ezek 30:17).

name: Calno (Calneh)
eraNotes: Kullania, conquered by Tiglath-pileser III (Isa 10:9; Amos 6:2). Calneh in Shinar (Gen 10:10) is a different place.

name: Chebar (Kebar)
modernName: Nar Kabari canal near Nippur, Iraq
eraNotes: Judean exile settlement where Ezekiel saw his visions (Ezek 1:1, 3, 3:15, 23, 10:15, 43:3). WEB renders Tel-abib as 'Tel Aviv' (Ezek 3:15).

name: Dumah
eraNotes: Oasis named in the oracle Isa 21:11. A Judean town Dumah (Josh 15:52) also exists.

name: Plain of Dura
eraNotes: Site of Nebuchadnezzar's golden image (Dan 3:1).

name: Gomorrah
eraNotes: Paired with Sodom as a byword for judgement.

name: Greece
eraNotes: 'Javan' (Isa 66:19; Ezek 27:13; Zech 9:13) = Ionian Greeks; Dan 8:21, 10:20, 11:2; Acts 20:2. Javan is also a person (Gen 10:2).

name: Hadrach
eraNotes: Assyrian Hatarikka (Zech 9:1).

name: Hanes
eraNotes: Egyptian city receiving Judah's envoys (Isa 30:4).

name: Hauran
eraNotes: Region east of the Jordan (Ezek 47:16, 18).

name: Helbon
eraNotes: Wine town trading with Tyre (Ezek 27:18).

name: Horonaim
eraNotes: Moabite town on a descent (Isa 15:5; Jer 48:3, 5, 34).

name: Jahaz
eraNotes: Moabite town on the steppe edge (Isa 15:4; Jer 48:21, 34).

name: Judah
modernName: Judean highlands and Shephelah (southern Israel / West Bank)
eraNotes: Southern kingdom (capital Jerusalem); matches kingdoms.json feature 'judah'. 'Judah' is also the patriarch/tribe (Gen 29–50; Matt 1; Luke 3; Heb 7:14; Rev 5:5, 7:5).

name: Kedar
eraNotes: Qedarite Arab tribal confederation (Isa 21:16, 42:11, 60:7; Jer 2:10, 49:28; Ezek 27:21).

name: Kerioth
eraNotes: Moabite city (Jer 48:24, 41; Amos 2:2).

name: Kiriathaim
eraNotes: Moabite town (Jer 48:1, 23; Ezek 25:9).

name: Libya (Put)
eraNotes: Put/Libya (Jer 46:9; Ezek 27:10, 30:5, 38:5; Nah 3:9; Acts 2:10). WEB's 'Put' is not aliased: the matcher is case-insensitive and would hit the verb 'put'.

name: Lud
eraNotes: Usually Lydia (Isa 66:19; Jer 46:9; Ezek 27:10, 30:5). The NT woman Lydia is deliberately not an alias.

name: Magog
eraNotes: Land of Gog (Ezek 38:2, 39:6); symbolic in Rev 20:8. Location unknown — pin is indicative only.

name: Mephaath
eraNotes: Moabite plateau town (Jer 48:21).

name: Meshech
eraNotes: Anatolian people paired with Tubal (Ezek 27:13, 32:26, 38:2–3, 39:1).

name: Migdol (Egypt)
eraNotes: Frontier fort with a Judean colony (Jer 44:1, 46:14; Ezek 29:10, 30:6). The Exodus Migdol (Exod 14:2) may be a different site.

name: Minni (Mannea)
modernName: South of Lake Urmia, north-western Iran
eraNotes: Mannean kingdom summoned against Babylon (Jer 51:27).

name: Moresheth-gath
eraNotes: Micah's hometown (Mic 1:1, 14; Jer 26:18).

name: Waters of Nimrim
eraNotes: Moabite oasis (Isa 15:6; Jer 48:34).

name: Pathros
eraNotes: Upper Egypt (Isa 11:11; Jer 44:1, 15; Ezek 29:14, 30:14).

name: Pelusium
eraNotes: 'Sin, the stronghold of Egypt' (Ezek 30:15–16); 'Sin' cannot be aliased.

name: Peor
eraNotes: Site of the Baal-peor apostasy (Num 25; Hos 9:10).

name: Raamah
eraNotes: Arabian trading people (Ezek 27:22).

name: Seba
eraNotes: Paired with Cush/Egypt (Isa 43:3, 45:14). Location debated.

name: Sibmah
eraNotes: Vineyard town (Isa 16:8–9; Jer 48:32).

name: Siloam
modernName: Pool of Siloam, City of David, Jerusalem
eraNotes: Hezekiah-tunnel pool (Isa 8:6, 22:9–11); tower (Luke 13:4); healing of the blind man (John 9:7).

name: Sodom
modernName: Southern Dead Sea basin (traditional; Tall el-Hammam north-east is an alternative)
eraNotes: Cities of the plain; proverbial for judgement (Isa 1:9–10; Jer 23:14; Ezek 16; Matt 10:15; Rom 9:29; 2 Pet 2:6; Jude 7).

name: Syene
eraNotes: Egypt's southern frontier (Ezek 29:10, 30:6). 'Land of Sinim' (Isa 49:12) is read as Syene (1QIsaᵃ).

name: Tahpanhes
eraNotes: Border fortress where Jeremiah was taken (Jer 2:16, 43:7–9, 44:1, 46:14; Ezek 30:18).

name: Tamar
eraNotes: South-eastern border point (Ezek 47:19, 48:28). Bare 'Tamar' is not aliased because it is a common personal name.

name: Tema
eraNotes: North-Arabian oasis (Isa 21:14; Jer 25:23); Nabonidus resided there.

name: Teman
eraNotes: Edomite district (Jer 49:7, 20; Ezek 25:13; Amos 1:12; Obad 9; Hab 3:3).

name: Togarmah
eraNotes: Horse-trading people 'in the uttermost parts of the north' (Ezek 27:14, 38:6).

name: Tubal
eraNotes: Anatolian people/land paired with Meshech (Isa 66:19; Ezek 27:13, 32:26, 38–39). Also a person (Gen 10:2).

name: Ulai
eraNotes: Setting of Daniel's ram-and-goat vision (Dan 8:2, 16).

name: Uz
eraNotes: Job's homeland; associated with Edom (Lam 4:21; Jer 25:20).

name: Zebulun
modernName: Lower Galilee hills west of Nazareth
eraNotes: Tribal territory of Lower Galilee; 'land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali' (Isa 9:1; Matt 4:13–15).

name: Zedad
eraNotes: Northern border point (Ezek 47:15; Num 34:8).

name: Abilene
eraNotes: Tetrarchy of Lysanias (Luke 3:1).

name: Achaia
eraNotes: Roman province governed from Corinth (Acts 18:12, 27; Rom 15:26; 2 Cor 1:1, 9:2; 1 Thess 1:7–8).

name: Adramyttium
eraNotes: Home port of Paul's first ship (Acts 27:2).

name: Sea of Adria
eraNotes: Ancient name for the central Mediterranean between Crete, Sicily and Greece (Acts 27:27).

name: Aenon near Salim
eraNotes: John baptizing 'because there was much water there' (John 3:23). 'Enon' also occurs inside 'Hazar Enon' (Ezek 47:17).

name: Akeldama (Field of Blood)
eraNotes: Field bought with Judas's silver (Matt 27:7–10; Acts 1:19).

name: Amphipolis
eraNotes: On the Via Egnatia (Acts 17:1).

name: Apollonia
eraNotes: On the Via Egnatia (Acts 17:1).

name: Areopagus (Mars Hill)
eraNotes: Paul's address (Acts 17:19–34).

name: Arimathea
eraNotes: Hometown of Joseph who buried Jesus (Matt 27:57; Mark 15:43; Luke 23:51; John 19:38).

name: Asia (Roman province)
eraNotes: Roman province governed from Ephesus (Acts 2:9, 16:6, 19:10, 20:16; 1 Cor 16:19; 2 Cor 1:8; 2 Tim 1:15; 1 Pet 1:1; Rev 1:4).

name: Assos
eraNotes: Paul walked from Troas to Assos (Acts 20:13–14).

name: Pool of Bethesda
modernName: St Anne's, Old City of Jerusalem
eraNotes: Healing at the pool (John 5:2).

name: Bithynia
eraNotes: Province Paul was prevented from entering (Acts 16:7; 1 Pet 1:1).

name: Cappadocia
eraNotes: Acts 2:9; 1 Pet 1:1.

name: Cauda (Clauda)
eraNotes: Islet where the lifeboat was secured (Acts 27:16).

name: Chios
eraNotes: Acts 20:15.

name: Cilicia
eraNotes: Paul's home province around Tarsus (Acts 6:9, 15:23, 41, 21:39, 22:3, 23:34, 27:5; Gal 1:21).

name: Cnidus
eraNotes: Acts 27:7.

name: Cos
eraNotes: Acts 21:1.

name: Cyrene
eraNotes: Home of Simon who carried the cross (Matt 27:32) and of early evangelists (Acts 11:20, 13:1).

name: Dalmatia
eraNotes: Titus went there (2 Tim 4:10).

name: Decapolis
eraNotes: League of Hellenistic cities east of the Jordan (Matt 4:25; Mark 5:20, 7:31).

name: Ephraim (town)
eraNotes: Town near the wilderness where Jesus withdrew (John 11:54).

name: Forum of Appius
eraNotes: Roman believers met Paul here (Acts 28:15).

name: Gadara
eraNotes: Decapolis city whose territory reached the lake (Matt 8:28; Mark 5:1; Luke 8:26 variants).

name: Galatia
eraNotes: Roman province (Acts 16:6, 18:23; 1 Cor 16:1; Gal 1:2; 2 Tim 4:10; 1 Pet 1:1).

name: Gennesaret
modernName: Ginosar plain, north-west shore of the lake
eraNotes: Fertile plain (Matt 14:34; Mark 6:53). 'Lake of Gennesaret' stays with galilee_sea.

name: Gergesa (Kursi)
modernName: Kursi, east shore of the Sea of Galilee
eraNotes: Lakeside site of the demoniac healing (Matt 8:28–34; Mark 5:1–20; Luke 8:26–39). The city Gerasa (Jerash) lies far to the south-east.

name: Gethsemane
modernName: Foot of the Mount of Olives, Jerusalem
eraNotes: Garden of the arrest (Matt 26:36; Mark 14:32; John 18:1).

name: Hierapolis
eraNotes: Lycus valley church (Col 4:13).

name: Idumea
eraNotes: Hellenistic–Roman Idumea south of Judea (Mark 3:8).

name: Illyricum
eraNotes: Limit of Paul's preaching (Rom 15:19).

name: Iturea
eraNotes: Part of Philip's tetrarchy (Luke 3:1).

name: Judea
eraNotes: Roman district around Jerusalem (Gospels, Acts).

name: Wilderness of Judea
eraNotes: John the Baptist's preaching ground (Matt 3:1); traditional temptation setting.

name: Lasea
modernName: South coast of Crete near Kaloi Limenes
eraNotes: City near Fair Havens (Acts 27:8).

name: Lycaonia
eraNotes: District of Lystra and Derbe (Acts 14:6, 11).

name: Lycia
eraNotes: District of Myra and Patara (Acts 27:5).

name: Macedonia
eraNotes: Roman province (Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea); Acts 16:9–12, 19:21, 20:1–3; Rom 15:26; 2 Cor 7–9; Phil 4:15.

name: Magdala
modernName: Migdal, west shore of the Sea of Galilee
eraNotes: Fishing town (Matt 15:39). 'Dalmanutha' (Mark 8:10) is unlocated and grouped here. 'Magdalene' is not aliased (personal epithet).

name: Miletus
eraNotes: Farewell to the Ephesian elders (Acts 20:15–38); 2 Tim 4:20.

name: Mitylene
eraNotes: Acts 20:14.

name: Mysia
eraNotes: Region passed through to Troas (Acts 16:7–8).

name: Neapolis
eraNotes: Port of Philippi (Acts 16:11).

name: Nicopolis
eraNotes: Paul planned to winter there (Titus 3:12).

name: Pamphylia
eraNotes: Coastal district of Perga and Attalia (Acts 2:10, 13:13, 14:24, 15:38, 27:5).

name: Parthia
eraNotes: Parthian empire (Acts 2:9).

name: Patara
eraNotes: Change of ship for Phoenicia (Acts 21:1–2).

name: Perea (beyond the Jordan)
eraNotes: Herod Antipas's Transjordan district (Matt 19:1; Mark 10:1); 'beyond the Jordan' (Isa 9:1; Matt 4:15, 25; Mark 3:8).

name: Phoenicia
eraNotes: Coastal city-states of Tyre, Sidon, Byblos and Arvad; matches kingdoms.json feature 'phoenicia'. Named in Acts 11:19, 15:3, 21:2.

name: Phoenix (Crete)
eraNotes: Intended winter harbour (Acts 27:12). KJV 'Phenice' is not aliased because KJV also uses it for Phoenicia.

name: Phrygia
eraNotes: Region crossed on the 2nd and 3rd journeys (Acts 2:10, 16:6, 18:23).

name: Pisidia
eraNotes: Mountain district (Acts 13:14, 14:24).

name: Pontus
modernName: Black Sea coast of north-eastern Turkey
eraNotes: Home of Aquila (Acts 18:2); Acts 2:9; 1 Pet 1:1.

name: Rhegium
eraNotes: Acts 28:13.

name: Rhodes
eraNotes: Acts 21:1.

name: Salmone
eraNotes: Acts 27:7.

name: Samaria (region)
eraNotes: Region between Judea and Galilee (Luke 17:11; John 4; Acts 1:8, 8:1, 9:31, 15:3). Bare 'Samaria' currently resolves to the city samaria_city.

name: Samos
eraNotes: Acts 20:15.

name: Samothrace
eraNotes: Overnight anchorage (Acts 16:11).

name: Spain
eraNotes: Paul's planned mission (Rom 15:24, 28).

name: Syracuse
eraNotes: Three-day stay (Acts 28:12).

name: Syria (Roman province)
eraNotes: Roman province governed from Antioch (Matt 4:24; Luke 2:2; Acts 15:23, 41, 18:18, 20:3, 21:3; Gal 1:21). Bare 'Syria' currently resolves to aram.

name: Syrtis
eraNotes: Shoals the sailors feared (Acts 27:17).

name: Three Taverns
eraNotes: Second welcoming party (Acts 28:15).

name: Tiberias
eraNotes: Herod Antipas's capital (John 6:23). 'Sea of Tiberias' stays with galilee_sea.

name: Trachonitis
eraNotes: Part of Philip's tetrarchy (Luke 3:1).

name: Abdon
eraNotes: Levitical city in Asher (Josh 21:30; 1 Chr 6:74); = Ebron of Josh 19:28 in some MSS. Joshua 21:30; 1 Chronicles 6:74

name: Accad
eraNotes: Genesis 10:10; one of Nimrod's cities in Shinar. Approx. site: Capital of Sargon's Akkadian empire; site not found, usually sought near Sippar/Baghdad on the Tigris-Euphrates.

name: Achmetha
eraNotes: Ezra 6:2; Median capital where Cyrus's decree was found.

name: Achshaph
eraNotes: Canaanite city allied with Jabin (Josh 11:1); king defeated (Josh 12:20); border of Asher (Josh 19:25). Joshua 11:1; Joshua 12:20; Joshua 19:25 Approx. site: Often identified with Tell Keisan; alternatives Khirbet el-Harbaj / Tell Regev.

name: Ascent of Adummim
modernName: Tal'at ed-Damm / Ma'ale Adummim pass on the Jerusalem-Jericho road
eraNotes: Boundary between Judah and Benjamin (Josh 15:7; 18:17). Joshua 15:7; Joshua 18:17

name: Ahlab
modernName: Khirbet el-Mahalib, NE of Tyre, Lebanon (proposed)
eraNotes: Canaanite town Asher failed to take (Judg 1:31); likely Mahalab of Josh 19:29. Judges 1:31; Joshua 19:29 Approx. site: Assyrian Mahalliba; usually placed at Khirbet el-Mahalib just north-east of Tyre.

name: Ascent of Akrabbim
modernName: Ma'ale Akrabim (Scorpion Pass), northern Negev, Israel
eraNotes: Southern border of Canaan/Judah (Num 34:4; Josh 15:3); Amorite border (Judg 1:36). Numbers 34:4; Joshua 15:3; Judges 1:36

name: Almon
eraNotes: Levitical city of Benjamin: Almon (Josh 21:18) = Alemeth (1 Chr 6:60). Joshua 21:18; 1 Chronicles 6:60

name: Amana
eraNotes: Song 4:8 (peak paired with Senir and Hermon); Qere 'Amana' river of 2 Kgs 5:12 (Abana). Song of Solomon 4:8 Approx. site: Usually the Anti-Lebanon peak/area at the source of the Barada (Abana); some prefer the Amanus range.

name: Anab
modernName: Khirbet 'Anab es-Saghir, SW of Hebron, West Bank
eraNotes: Anakim expelled from Anab (Josh 11:21); town of Judah's hill country (Josh 15:50). Joshua 11:21; Joshua 15:50

name: Anim
modernName: Khirbet Ghuwein et-Tahta (Horvat Anim), S of Hebron hills
eraNotes: Town in Judah's hill country (Josh 15:50). Joshua 15:50

name: Aphek (Asher)
modernName: Tel Afek (Tell Kurdaneh), near Kiryat Bialik, Israel
eraNotes: Asher town not conquered (Judg 1:31, 'Aphik'); in Asher's allotment (Josh 19:30). Judges 1:31; Joshua 19:30

name: Ascent of Akrabbim
eraNotes: Pass on the southern border of Canaan/Judah and the Amorite border. Num 34:4; Josh 15:3; Judg 1:36

name: Azmaveth
modernName: Hizma, NE of Jerusalem, West Bank
eraNotes: Returning exiles from Azmaveth/Beth-azmaveth (Ezra 2:24; Neh 7:28); singers' villages (Neh 12:29).

name: Beth-anoth
modernName: Beit 'Einun, NE of Hebron, West Bank
eraNotes: Town in Judah's hill country (Josh 15:59). Joshua 15:59

name: Beth-arabah
eraNotes: Boundary town between Judah and Benjamin (Josh 15:6, 61; 18:18, 22). Joshua 15:6; Joshua 15:61; Joshua 18:22 Approx. site: Generally placed at 'Ain el-Gharabeh in the lower Jordan valley near Jericho.

name: Beth-aram
modernName: Tell er-Rameh / Tell Iktanu, Jordan valley east of the Jordan
eraNotes: Gadite town in the Jordan valley (Josh 13:27); fortified by Gad as Beth-haran (Num 32:36). Joshua 13:27; Numbers 32:36 Approx. site: Later Livias/Julias; candidates Tell er-Rameh and nearby Tell Iktanu.

name: Beth-eked
eraNotes: Where Jehu slaughtered Ahaziah's kinsmen (2 Kgs 10:12-14). Approx. site: Beit Qad east of Jenin, on the Jezreel-Samaria road.

name: Beth-tappuah
modernName: Taffuh, W of Hebron, West Bank
eraNotes: Town in Judah's hill country (Josh 15:53). Joshua 15:53

name: Bethabara
modernName: Al-Maghtas (Baptism Site), east bank of the Jordan, Jordan
eraNotes: John 1:28 (KJV 'Bethabara'; most MSS 'Bethany beyond the Jordan'), where John baptized.

name: Bezer
modernName: Medeba plateau east of Madaba, Jordan (Umm el-'Amad or Tell Jalul proposed)
eraNotes: City of refuge of Reuben (Deut 4:43; Josh 20:8); Levitical city (Josh 21:36; 1 Chr 6:78). Deuteronomy 4:43; Joshua 20:8; Joshua 21:36 Approx. site: Mesha Stele 'Bosor'; candidates Umm el-'Amad and Tell Jalul, marker placed on the plateau be

name: Brook Kanah
eraNotes: Wadi forming the boundary between Ephraim and Manasseh. Josh 16:8; Josh 17:9

name: Chaldea
eraNotes: Southern Babylonia; Neo-Babylonian ruling people (Jer 50:10; Ezek 11:24; 16:29; 23:15). Jeremiah 50:10; Ezekiel 11:24; Ezekiel 23:15

name: Chesalon
eraNotes: Northern border of Judah, on the shoulder of Mount Jearim (Josh 15:10). Joshua 15:10

name: Chesulloth
eraNotes: Border town of Issachar (Josh 19:18) = Chisloth-tabor on Zebulun's border (Josh 19:12). Joshua 19:18; Joshua 19:12

name: Crete
eraNotes: Cretans at Pentecost (Acts 2:11); Paul sailed under Crete (Acts 27:7-21); Titus left in Crete (Titus 1:5).

name: Ecbatana
eraNotes: Median capital and Persian summer residence where Cyrus's decree was found (Ezra 6:2).

name: Eglon
eraNotes: Amorite city in the Shephelah whose king joined the southern coalition; later a town of Judah. Josh 10:3; Josh 10:34-35; Josh 12:12; Josh 15:39

name: Ellasar
eraNotes: Kingdom of Arioch, ally of Kedorlaomer in the campaign against the cities of the plain. Gen 14:1; Gen 14:9 Approx. site: Larsa is the common atlas identification; alternatives include Ilanzura (Upper Mesopotamia) and Telassar.

name: En-eglaim
eraNotes: Spring on the Dead Sea shore in Ezekiel's vision of the healed waters (fishermen from En-gedi to En-eglaim). Ezek 47:10 Approx. site: Most often equated with 'Ein Feshkha; 'Ain Hajlah near the Jordan mouth also proposed.

name: En-rimmon
modernName: Kh. Umm er-Ramamin / Tel Halif area (proposed)
eraNotes: Southern town of Judah/Simeon, resettled after the exile (Josh 15:32; 19:7; Neh 11:29; Zech 14:10). Approx. site: Identification disputed between Kh. Umm er-Ramamin and nearby Tel Halif; both within a few km.

name: En-shemesh
modernName: 'Ain el-Hod ('Spring of the Apostles'), east of al-Eizariya
eraNotes: Spring on the Judah-Benjamin boundary on the descent from Jerusalem toward Jericho. Josh 15:7; Josh 18:17

name: Gath-rimmon
modernName: Tel Gerisa (Tell Jerisheh), Ramat Gan/Tel Aviv
eraNotes: Danite town assigned to the Kohathite Levites, on the Yarkon. Josh 19:45; Josh 21:24; 1 Chr 6:69 Approx. site: Tel Gerisa vs Tell Abu Zeitun both proposed. Josh 21:25 'Gath-rimmon' in Manasseh is likely a scribal slip for Ibleam/Bileam - no

name: Gedor
modernName: Khirbet Jedur, near Beit Ummar, West Bank
eraNotes: Town in the hill country of Judah between Bethlehem and Hebron. Josh 15:58 Approx. site: Pin for Judahite Gedor only (Khirbet Jedur). Gedor of Benjamin (1 Chr 12:7) and of Simeon (1 Chr 4:39) are separate/unlocated; also a personal name.

name: Gibeah (Judah)
eraNotes: Town in the hill country of Judah listed with Kain and Timnah. Josh 15:57 Approx. site: Tentative identification with Jab'a. Bare 'Gibeah' already resolves to Gibeah of Saul (gibeah).

name: Gibeah of Phinehas
modernName: Awarta, southeast of Nablus (traditional tomb of Eleazar)
eraNotes: Hill in the hill country of Ephraim where Eleazar son of Aaron was buried. Josh 24:33 Approx. site: Samaritan/Jewish tradition places Eleazar's tomb at Awarta; no archaeological confirmation.

name: Gimzo
eraNotes: Shephelah town captured by the Philistines in the reign of Ahaz. 2 Chr 28:18

name: Hadid
eraNotes: Town near Lod resettled by returning exiles. Ezra 2:33; Neh 7:37; Neh 11:34

name: Hazarmaveth
eraNotes: Joktanite people/region of South Arabia in the Table of Nations. Gen 10:26; 1 Chr 1:20

name: Hazeroth
eraNotes: Wilderness camp after Kibroth-hattaavah where Miriam and Aaron opposed Moses. Num 11:35; Num 12:16; Num 33:17-18; Deut 1:1 Approx. site: Traditional identification assumes the southern-Sinai route; unknown under other route models.

name: Hosah
eraNotes: Border point of Asher near Tyre. Josh 19:29 Approx. site: Equated with Assyrian Ushu (Palaetyrus) on the mainland opposite Tyre. 'Hosah' is also a Levite gatekeeper (1 Chr 16:38; 26:10).

name: Hukkok
modernName: Huqoq (Yaquq), northwest of the Sea of Galilee
eraNotes: Border town of Naphtali. Josh 19:34

name: India
eraNotes: Eastern limit of the Persian empire of Ahasuerus (Persian satrapy Hindush). Esth 1:1; Esth 8:9

name: Jacob's Well
eraNotes: Well at Sychar where Jesus spoke with the Samaritan woman, on the parcel Jacob gave Joseph. John 4:5-6; Gen 33:19; Josh 24:32

name: Juttah
modernName: Yatta, south of Hebron, West Bank
eraNotes: Hill-country town of Judah given to the Levites. Josh 15:55; Josh 21:16

name: Kain
modernName: Khirbet Yaqin / Nebi Yaqin, near Bani Na'im, West Bank
eraNotes: Town of Judah (Josh 15:57; KJV 'Cain'). Joshua 15:57 Approx. site: 'Cain' deliberately omitted as alias (collides with Adam's son); site at Nebi Yaqin SE of Hebron.

name: Kanah (Asher)
eraNotes: Town on the border of Asher, as far as Great Sidon. Josh 19:28

name: Kinah
eraNotes: Town of Judah's Negeb district near the Edomite border. Josh 15:22 Approx. site: Aharoni/Rainey link Kinah to Wadi el-Qeini and Horvat 'Uza east of Arad; site identification and coords approximate.

name: Kishion
modernName: Tel Qishyon, SE of Mount Tabor (proposed)
eraNotes: Issachar town given to the Gershonite Levites (KJV 'Kishon' in Josh 21:28). Josh 19:20; Josh 21:28 Approx. site: Bare 'Kishon' deliberately not aliased (collides with brook Kishon). Coords approximate for Tel Qishyon.

name: Madon
eraNotes: Canaanite city whose king Jobab joined Jabin's northern coalition. Josh 11:1; Josh 12:19 Approx. site: Usually placed at Tel Qarnei Hittin; LXX reads 'Maron' (possibly Merom), so identification is uncertain.

name: Makkedah
eraNotes: Cave where Joshua trapped the five Amorite kings; town of the Shephelah. Josh 10:10; Josh 10:16-28; Josh 12:16; Josh 15:41 Approx. site: Dorsey's Kh. el-Qom identification is widely followed; Tel Bornat and others also proposed.

name: Me-jarkon
eraNotes: Boundary water of Dan's inheritance near Joppa. Josh 19:46

name: Migdal-eder
modernName: Beit Sahour (Shepherds' Field tradition), near Bethlehem
eraNotes: Israel (Jacob) camped beyond it after Rachel's death; Micah's 'tower of the flock'. Gen 35:21; Mic 4:8 Approx. site: Located only by tradition between Bethlehem and Hebron/Jerusalem; pin at Beit Sahour tradition.

name: Migdal Eder (Tower of Edar)
eraNotes: Israel (Jacob) camped beyond the tower of Edar after Rachel's death near Bethlehem; Micah's 'tower of the flock'. Gen 35:21; Mic 4:8 Approx. site: Traditional (Jerome) location c. 1 Roman mile from Bethlehem; exact site unknown. Bare 'Eder'

name: Misrephoth-maim
eraNotes: Limit of Joshua's pursuit after Merom; northern border of unconquered land near Sidon. Josh 11:8; Josh 13:6 Approx. site: Coastal site below Rosh HaNikra commonly proposed; some identify with the Litani River.

name: Mount Hor
eraNotes: Mountain on the border of Edom where Aaron died and was buried. Num 20:22-28; Num 21:4; Num 33:37-41; Deut 32:50 Approx. site: Traditional Jebel Harun; Jebel Madurah NE of Kadesh is the main alternative. The northern 'Mount Hor' of Num 34:7

name: Mount Jearim
modernName: Kesla / Kesalon ridge, west of Jerusalem
eraNotes: Ridge on Judah's northern border, 'which is Chesalon'. Josh 15:10 Approx. site: Chesalon = Kesla is standard; the pin marks the ridge at Chesalon. Distinct from Kiriath-jearim.

name: Mozah
eraNotes: Benjamite town; Iron Age temple excavated at Tel Moza. Josh 18:26

name: Naarah
modernName: Tell el-Jisr near 'Ain Duk / Na'aran, N of Jericho (proposed)
eraNotes: Town on Ephraim's eastern border near Jericho. Josh 16:7; 1 Chr 7:28 Approx. site: Roman-era Na'aran (synagogue at 'Ain Duk) preserves the name; Iron Age site uncertain.

name: Neballat
modernName: Beit Nabala (former village), NE of Lod
eraNotes: Benjamite settlement of returning exiles near Lod and Ono. Neh 11:34

name: Waters of Nephtoah
aliases: fountain of the waters of Nephtoah
modernName: Lifta (Mei Neftoah), W edge of Jerusalem
eraNotes: Spring on the Judah-Benjamin boundary. Josh 15:9; Josh 18:15

name: Nezib
modernName: Khirbet Beit Nesib, NW of Hebron
eraNotes: Town of the Judean Shephelah. Josh 15:43 Approx. site: Name preserved at Kh. Beit Nesib; coords approximate.

name: Ophel
modernName: Ophel ridge, between City of David and Temple Mount, Jerusalem
eraNotes: Fortified ridge of Jerusalem; walls built by Jotham and Manasseh; temple servants lived here. 2 Chr 27:3; 2 Chr 33:14; Neh 3:26-27; Neh 11:21; Isa 32:14; Mic 4:8

name: Ophni
eraNotes: Town of Benjamin. Josh 18:24 Approx. site: Commonly equated with Roman Gophna (Jifna).

name: Parah
modernName: Khirbet el-Fara / Ein Prat, Wadi Qelt
eraNotes: Town of Benjamin. Josh 18:23

name: Pethor
modernName: Pitru, near Sajur-Euphrates confluence, N Syria (proposed)
eraNotes: Hometown of Balaam 'by the river' in Aram-naharaim. Num 22:5; Deut 23:4 Approx. site: Assyrian Pitru south of Carchemish; exact tell uncertain.

name: Pirathon
eraNotes: Home and burial place of judge Abdon; home of David's warrior Benaiah. Judg 12:13; Judg 12:15; 2 Sam 23:30; 1 Chr 11:31; 1 Chr 27:14 Approx. site: Far'ata preserves the name; coords approximate.

name: Rehoboth (well)
eraNotes: Well dug by Isaac's servants near Gerar. Gen 26:22 Approx. site: Distinct from Rehoboth-Ir in Assyria (Gen 10:11) and 'Rehoboth by the river' (Gen 36:37); the bare alias may also match those.

name: Resen
eraNotes: Assyrian city built by Nimrod's line between Nineveh and Calah (Gen 10:12). Approx. site: Unlocated; placed between Nineveh and Calah per the text. Selamiyeh near Nimrud has been proposed.

name: Rock of Rimmon
eraNotes: Refuge of 600 Benjaminites after Gibeah (Judg 20:45-47; 21:13).

name: Rimmon (Zebulun)
modernName: Rummana, N edge of the Beit Netofa Valley
eraNotes: Border town of Zebulun; Levitical city. Josh 19:13; 1 Chr 6:77

name: Rumah
eraNotes: Hometown of Zebudah, mother of King Jehoiakim (2 Kgs 23:36).

name: Sansannah
eraNotes: Southern town of Judah; probably = Hazar-susah of Simeon (Josh 15:31). Approx. site: Proposed site NE of Beersheba basin; tentative.

name: Secacah
eraNotes: Wilderness town of Judah (Josh 15:61). Approx. site: One of six wilderness towns usually placed in the Buqei'a; Qumran also proposed (~8 km E).

name: Sela-hammahlekoth
eraNotes: Rock where Saul broke off pursuit of David (1 Sam 23:28). Approx. site: In the Wilderness of Maon; gorge identification tentative.

name: Seneh
eraNotes: Rocky crag opposite Bozez in the pass of Michmash (1 Sam 14:4-5).

name: Sephar
eraNotes: Eastern limit of the Joktanite peoples (Gen 10:30). Approx. site: Traditionally Zafar, Himyarite capital; conjectural.

name: Shaaraim
eraNotes: Shephelah town of Judah on the road of the Philistine retreat after Goliath (Josh 15:36; 1 Sam 17:52).

name: Shalem
eraNotes: Jacob came to 'Shalem, a city of Shechem' (Gen 33:18 KJV). Approx. site: Many versions read 'safely to the city of Shechem'; Salim village 5 km E of Shechem keeps the name.

name: Shaphir
eraNotes: Town in Micah's lament over the Shephelah (Mic 1:11). Approx. site: Name echo at es-Sawafir; a site nearer Lachish/Moresheth is also proposed.

name: Well of Sirah
eraNotes: Where Joab's messengers recalled Abner before killing him (2 Sam 3:26).

name: Taanath-shiloh
eraNotes: Border point of Ephraim east of Michmethath (Josh 16:6).

name: Tappuah
modernName: Tell Sheikh Abu Zarad, West Bank
eraNotes: Border town between Ephraim and Manasseh; its king defeated by Joshua (Josh 12:17; 16:8; 17:7-8).

name: Thebez
eraNotes: Abimelech killed by a millstone dropped from its tower (Judg 9:50-53; 2 Sam 11:21).

name: Tophel
eraNotes: Landmark where Moses spoke beyond the Jordan (Deut 1:1).

name: Trogyllium
eraNotes: Paul's ship tarried here between Samos and Miletus (Acts 20:15, KJV/TR).

name: Uzzen-sheerah
eraNotes: Town built by Sheerah, daughter of Ephraim, with the Beth-horons (1 Chr 7:24). Approx. site: Beit Sira just west of Lower Beth-horon; name similarity.

name: Valley of Shaveh
eraNotes: Where Melchizedek met Abram; the King's Valley of Absalom's pillar (Gen 14:17; 2 Sam 18:18). Approx. site: Josephus puts Absalom's monument 2 stadia from Jerusalem; exact valley uncertain.

name: Valley of Siddim
eraNotes: Battle of the four kings against five; full of bitumen pits (Gen 14:3, 8, 10). Approx. site: Text equates it with the Salt Sea; placed in the shallow southern basin.

name: Waters of Merom
eraNotes: Joshua's defeat of Jabin's northern coalition. Josh 11:5; Josh 11:7 Approx. site: Older maps use Lake Huleh; many modern atlases prefer springs near Meiron. Site disputed.

name: Zanoah
eraNotes: Shephelah town of Judah, resettled after the exile; its men repaired the Valley Gate (Josh 15:34; Neh 3:13; 11:30).

name: Zereth-shahar
eraNotes: Reubenite town 'on the hill of the valley' (Josh 13:19). Approx. site: East shore of the Dead Sea near Machaerus; tentative.

name: Valley of Zephathah
eraNotes: Asa defeated Zerah the Cushite 'in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah' (2 Chr 14:10). Approx. site: Text ties it to Mareshah; valley itself not pinpointed.

name: Zior
eraNotes: Hill-country town of Judah (Josh 15:54).

name: Ascent of Ziz
eraNotes: Pass by which Moab and Ammon came up against Jehoshaphat (2 Chr 20:16). Approx. site: Ascent from En-gedi toward Tekoa; usually Wadi Hasasa.

name: Stone of Zoheleth
eraNotes: Where Adonijah held his feast by En-rogel (1 Kgs 1:9).
